news.headline: Delcath Systems Amends Bylaws to Designate Delaware Courts as Exclusive Forum
news.summary: The board amended and restated Delcath's bylaws effective 2026-08-12, making Delaware's Court of Chancery the exclusive forum for internal corporate claims and U.S. federal courts the forum for Securities Act claims. It is a routine governance update for a Delaware-incorporated company, recommended by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.

news.headline: Delcath Hits Fresh 12-Month High Above $17 as Analysts Lift Targets After Q2 Beat
news.summary: DCTH pushed to a new 52-week high above $17 (market cap roughly $595M) as the post-earnings rally extended, after BTIG raised its target to $21 from $17 and H.C. Wainwright to $32 from $30, both Buy. The stock has held broadly in the mid-to-high $17 range through mid-August, with short interest also climbing roughly 29% into late July as bears pushed back against the rally.

news.headline: Delcath Systems Presents at Canaccord Genuity 46th Annual Growth Conference in Boston
news.summary: Management presented to institutional investors in Boston five days after the Q2 beat, using the slot to reinforce the HEPZATO KIT commercial-ramp story and the center-activation roadmap toward roughly 37 active centers. Investor outreach at growth conferences has been a consistent part of the post-approval narrative build.

news.headline: Q2 Call: mCRC Phase 2 Screening at 13 Centers, FDA Pre-IND Meetings Planned for Additional Indications
news.summary: On the Q2 call management said the company-sponsored Phase 2 trial of HEPZATO in metastatic colorectal cancer now has 13 centers actively screening, and that it plans pre-IND meetings with the FDA later in 2026 to discuss further liver-dominant indications beyond the mCRC and breast cancer programs already underway. Management also cited independent ESMO Breast Cancer 2026 data showing a 60% hepatic partial response rate with percutaneous hepatic perfusion in heavily pretreated liver-dominant metastatic breast cancer.

news.headline: Delcath Reports Q2 2026: $29.1M Revenue Beats Estimates, FY Guidance Raised to $104M-$108M
news.summary: Total revenue rose to $29.1M from $24.2M a year earlier (HEPZATO KIT $27.1M, CHEMOSAT $2.0M) on roughly 30% HEPZATO volume growth, with gross margin expanding to 90% from 86%, net income of $2.7M and EPS of $0.07 versus a consensus loss of $0.09; two new centers were activated in the quarter, including MD Anderson and Mayo Clinic Scottsdale, bringing the active total to 31 toward a year-end target of 37. Delcath raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $104M-$108M and reiterated its expectation of positive adjusted EBITDA for the year, though management flagged that 340B pricing introduced in mid-2025 continues to hold revenue growth below volume growth; the stock jumped more than 20% on the print, its best day since May 2025.

news.headline: First Patient Dosed in DELUMA Phase 2 of HEPZATO in Liver-Dominant Metastatic Breast Cancer
news.summary: The first patient was dosed at the European Institute of Oncology in Milan in the roughly 90-patient randomized DELUMA trial (NCT06875128), testing HEPZATO plus standard of care in HER2-negative liver-dominant metastatic breast cancer. It is the company's key pipeline expansion beyond ocular melanoma into a far larger addressable indication.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: The next quarterly report is expected in early-to-mid November 2026 based on prior-year timing; no exact date has been announced yet. It is the first checkpoint on whether HEPZATO volume growth and center activations are tracking the raised full-year guidance.

catalysts.label: 37 active HEPZATO treatment centers
catalysts.detail: Delcath exited Q2 2026 with 31 active HEPZATO KIT centers, including newly activated MD Anderson and Mayo Clinic Scottsdale, and targets roughly 37 by year-end. Center count is the most direct driver of near-term revenue, so the pace of the final activations is the key operational metric to watch.

catalysts.label: FY2026 revenue $104M-$108M and positive adjusted EBITDA
catalysts.detail: Raised guidance implies at least 28% HEPZATO volume growth over 2025 with gross margin around 90%, though 340B pricing introduced in mid-2025 continues to cap revenue growth below volume growth. Management also guided to positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year, which would mark the transition to a self-funding commercial model.

catalysts.label: mCRC Phase 2 enrollment progress
catalysts.detail: The company-sponsored Phase 2 trial of HEPZATO in metastatic colorectal cancer had 13 centers actively screening as of the Q2 call, with recruitment improving. Enrollment milestones and eventual data would open the largest liver-dominant indication in the pipeline.

catalysts.label: FDA pre-IND meetings for additional liver-dominant indications
catalysts.detail: Management said on the Q2 call it plans pre-IND meetings with the FDA later in 2026 to discuss further liver-dominant indications beyond the ongoing mCRC and breast cancer Phase 2 programs, each estimated at 6,000-10,000 U.S. patients annually in the third-line setting. Outcomes would signal which indication(s) the company pursues next for formal trials.

catalysts.label: DELUMA breast cancer Phase 2 enrollment and data
catalysts.detail: The roughly 90-patient randomized Phase 2 in HER2-negative liver-dominant metastatic breast cancer began dosing in July 2026 and is enrolling across US and EU sites. Full enrollment and first efficacy readouts are the next major pipeline catalysts, supported by independent ESMO retrospective data showing a 60% hepatic partial response rate.

pulse: Delcath remains in the strongest stretch of its commercial story: Q2 2026 revenue of $29.1M beat estimates, gross margin hit 90%, EPS flipped to $0.07 against an expected loss, and full-year guidance was lifted to $104M-$108M with positive adjusted EBITDA expected, while two prestigious new centers (MD Anderson, Mayo Clinic Scottsdale) joined the network. The stock jumped over 20% on the print and pushed to fresh 52-week highs above $17, holding that range through mid-August even as short interest climbed roughly 29% into late July, with sell-side targets from BTIG ($21) and H.C. Wainwright ($32) still well above the current price; no material company-specific news has emerged since the mid-August bylaws housekeeping filing. The near-term story is pure execution -- getting from 31 to 37 active HEPZATO centers by year-end and offsetting the 340B pricing headwind -- while the DELUMA breast cancer Phase 2, the 13-center mCRC Phase 2, and planned FDA pre-IND meetings for further indications carry the longer-dated optionality beyond ocular melanoma.
